_comment: Single source of truth for the versions CI builds, tests and verifies against. Read by the
test-matrix job in .github/workflows/shared-test.yml, which composes the test legs and the
plugin-verification legs, and by .github/actions/setup-env, which fills any version input left
empty so the release/tag/build-plugin jobs need not restate the minimum supported platform.
Find available IDE versions at https://www.jetbrains.com/idea/download/other/ and
https://www.jetbrains.com/ruby/download/other/
Things you cannot tell from the values themselves:
idea.minimumSupported.version must be the marketing version that gradle.properties'
pluginSinceBuild pins.
java must be the JBR level the platform's JARs are compiled for - build.gradle.kts derives the
same value from the build number, and a wrong one fails the compile rather than the tests,
because javac --release validates the class-file version of everything on the classpath.
verify values are intellij-repository artifact ids, not marketing names: ideaIU, ideaIC,
pycharmPC, pycharmPY, goland, clion, phpstorm, rubymine, webstorm, mps, riderRD, riderRS.
RustRover is published but unusable - the verifier action derives the repository directory
from the id's lowercase prefix, and that id starts with a capital. List a product only for
versions JetBrains has published it for; they lag IDEA on new majors. This affects
verification only: test legs always build against IntelliJ IDEA.
Declaring anything twice is an error, not a second configuration: the generator fails naming
the duplicate, because every leg name has to be unique within a run. A second entry for a
version, or a product listed twice under one version, will stop the matrix before it runs.
beam.baseline must match the mise.toml pin, and must stay green.
beam.additional is a ratchet. continue-on-error means the version is NOT supported yet and its
leg is expected to fail; the workflow tolerates failure at every phase of that leg, not just
the tests, so an Elixir the toolchain or the quoter cannot handle still cannot block a merge.
Delete the flag once the leg is green - the version is then supported, and any later change
that breaks it fails the pipeline.
Check OTP support against https://elixir.hexdocs.pm/compatibility-and-deprecations.html, which
is patch-aware: 1.14 is '23 - 25 (and Erlang/OTP 26 from v1.14.5)'. Do NOT use otp_versions
from elixir-lang.github.com's _data/elixir-versions.yml to decide the range - it is per-MINOR
and misses OTP support added in a patch. Within the range prefer that file's recommended_otp.
A pair may also exist to cover an OTP major no other pair covers - ~75% of the swept BEAM surface
is Erlang and the chunk formats track OTP, not Elixir - so the same Elixir may appear twice with
different OTPs. Read by OTP major the pairs below are {24, 25, 26, 27, 28}. Prefer the cleanest
in-window Elixir for such a leg so it isolates the OTP surface instead of inheriting a quoting
backlog.
